turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: I finally moved into the second-floor apartment by the bakery. It is quieter than the old place and I can work without hearing the street noise.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That sounds like the right trade-off. You were so drained by the last flat.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Exactly. I also adopted a rescue dog named Biscuit. He follows me from room to room like a tiny security guard.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: Biscuit is a perfect name. Is he still trying to steal every sock?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Always. And I am starting a remote-first role at Northwind Labs this week. I need a stable routine for deep work.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: Good idea. Does your schedule still let you keep mornings calm?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Yes, I work best without early meeting pressure. I am protecting my first two hours for focused writing and design work.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: I switched to a mostly plant-based diet, mostly for energy and digestion, but I still keep a Friday cheat meal for pizza.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That is a solid balance. What did the first two weeks feel like?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Better, honestly. Even the afternoon slump is lighter. Biscuit also got into my basil pot and somehow managed to look innocent.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That is such a Biscuit move. What is your favorite quick lunch now?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: A tofu grain bowl with roasted carrots and tahini. I keep it on repeat because it is fast and filling.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: Good call. It is the kind of meal that keeps a workday moving.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Right, and I also decided to stop taking breakfast meetings unless they are truly critical.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: I am finally planning the trip I wanted for months. Portland first, then Lisbon in June, if work stays manageable.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: Portland is such a good start. Are you keeping the Lisbon part?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: I want a quiet hotel with a balcony and a neighborhood walkable enough for late lunches. Lisbon still sounds lovely, but I do not want to rush it.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That sounds very you. Which part of the city are you thinking about?

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: I want to stay somewhere close to a tram stop and not too close to nightlife. I value sleep and nice coffee more than loud nights out.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That is a great rule. A slow trip is often better than a packed one.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Exactly. I can already picture the mornings: coffee on the balcony, a walk, and no rushing.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Work got busier than expected, so I canceled the Lisbon leg. I am still going to Portland next month, but only for a few nights.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That is a sensible call. I am glad you protected your energy instead of burning yourself out.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Thanks. The apartment is working well for me too. The light is better in the morning and I finally have a small desk by the window where I can think without the room feeling cramped.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That kind of setup really matters when you need focus.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: It does. Biscuit still sleeps under the desk, but now he steals my pens instead of the basil pot.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: That sounds like progress.

turns.speaker: Mara
turns.text: Very small progress, but still progress.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I signed up for the spring half-marathon in May. Training starts this week and I am trying to be consistent for once.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is great. What is the plan?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Three morning runs a week, plus a long weekend run every Saturday. I am trying to keep it sustainable rather than overdo it.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: Sound strategy. Are you still trying to keep your weekend mornings free?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Yes, that part is non-negotiable. My family visit is in Seattle in early June and I do not want to burn out before then.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That makes sense. A strong plan beats motivation alone.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Exactly. I have been taking my route by the river because it is easier on my knees.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I ran a ten-kilometer test and my shin started hurting after mile six. I had to cut it short and switch to bike intervals for a while.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is frustrating, but smart to back off. Did you lean into the rest?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I did. I am cross-training twice a week and doing mobility work before bed. I also stopped eating red meat most days after the trainer suggested a lighter recovery diet.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is a practical adjustment. Any improvement?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Some. I am not racing yet, but I am feeling more stable and less stiff.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is exactly what you want before a big event.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Right. I am trying to keep the goal realistic and protect long-term training.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is the mature approach.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: The half-marathon is in two weeks, and my taper is working. I ran a shorter route last weekend and felt strong, almost completely pain-free.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That is exactly what you wanted to hear. Are you still going to Seattle after the race?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Yes, I am taking the train out there right after. My cousins are hosting a barbecue, and my sister is already telling me to bring extra snacks.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: A post-race trip sounds like a nice reward.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: It will be. I have also been keeping my recovery meals simple — rice bowls, fruit, and more vegetables than before.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That fits the plan well.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: It does. I am much more deliberate than I used to be.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: The Seattle trip was great. I ran the race in a respectable time and then spent the next two days eating grilled food and walking around the waterfront.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That sounds like a perfect recovery week.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: It was. I have now shifted to an easier base-building block and I am planning a quieter summer with more consistent rest days.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That sounds like the right reset after the training cycle.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Exactly. The race was a success, but I do not want to chase intensity again immediately.

turns.speaker: Ramona
turns.text: That kind of discipline is what keeps people going.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I am learning that the hard way.
